source.text: יְשֻׂשׂ֥וּםמִדְבָּ֖ר וְצִיָּ֑ה וְתָגֵ֧ל עֲרָבָ֛ה וְתִפְרַ֖ח כַּחֲבַצָּֽלֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: Will be glad wilderness and dry-land, and will rejoice [the] desert-plain and blossom like [the] crocus.

en.L: [The] wilderness and [the] dry land will be glad, and [the] desert plain will rejoice and blossom like [the] crocus.
en.B: Wilderness and thirsty land will be glad; the barren plain will exult and break into flower like the crocus.
en.R: The desert and the dry land will be happy. The empty plains will be full of joy, and flowers will bloom there like crocuses.

decisions.choice: will be glad: the verb's final letter read as part of the form, not as "for them"
decisions.reason: The verb ends with a letter that can be a pronoun, giving "will be glad for them" (that is, because of the people of v. 10, or because of Edom's ruin in chapter 34). It may instead be the first letter of the next word written twice, or an old verb ending. The rejoicing land is the picture either way.

decisions.choice: crocus: a wild flower that springs up from a bulb
decisions.reason: The flower is named only here and in Song of Songs 2:1. It is a flower of the fields, perhaps a crocus, asphodel or narcissus; the familiar "rose" is a guess.

decisions.choice: the wilderness glad: a reversal of chapter 34
decisions.reason: Edom's land became a burning waste (34:9-10); now the dry land comes alive. The same reversal of wilderness into garden runs through 41:18-19, 43:19-20 and 51:3.

source.text: פָּרֹ֨חַ תִּפְרַ֜ח וְתָגֵ֗ל אַ֚ף גִּילַ֣ת וְרַנֵּ֔ן כְּב֤וֹד הַלְּבָנוֹן֙ נִתַּן־לָ֔הּ הֲדַ֥ר הַכַּרְמֶ֖ל וְהַשָּׁר֑וֹן הֵ֛מָּה יִרְא֥וּ כְבוֹד־יְהוָ֖ה הֲדַ֥ר אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Abundantly it will blossom and rejoice, even [with] rejoicing and shouting; the glory of the Lebanon will be given to it, the splendor of the Carmel and the Sharon; they will see [the] glory of the LORD, [the] splendor of our God.

en.L: It will blossom abundantly and rejoice, yes, [with] rejoicing and shouting for joy. The glory of Lebanon will be given to it, the splendor of Carmel and Sharon. They will see [the] glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, [the] splendor of our God.
en.B: Its blossoms will be everywhere; it will exult with gladness and glad cries. It will receive the glory of Lebanon, the splendor of Carmel and of Sharon. They will see {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory, our God in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} splendor.
en.R: Flowers will cover the land, and it will sing and shout for joy. It will be given the glory of Lebanon's forests and the beauty of the rich lands of Carmel and Sharon. People will see the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They will see how great our God is.

decisions.choice: Lebanon, Carmel, Sharon: the most fertile places in the land
decisions.reason: Lebanon was known for its cedars, Carmel for its wooded heights, and Sharon for its rich coastal plain. In 33:9 all three wither; here their beauty is given to the desert.

decisions.choice: they will see: people who see God's glory in the renewed land
decisions.reason: "They" is not named. It may be the people God brings home (vv. 4, 10), or the wilderness places themselves, pictured as seeing. Either way the glory of the land shows the glory of God (40:5).

decisions.choice: People will see ... how great our God is
decisions.reason: Readable names "they" as people and explains God's splendor as his greatness.

source.text: חַזְּק֖וּ יָדַ֣יִם רָפ֑וֹת וּבִרְכַּ֥יִם כֹּשְׁל֖וֹת אַמֵּֽצוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Strengthen hands slack, and knees stumbling make firm.

en.L: Strengthen slack hands, and make firm stumbling knees.
en.B: Put strength into hands that hang limp; steady the knees that buckle.
en.R: Help people whose hands are weak to be strong again. Help people whose knees are shaking to stand firm.

decisions.choice: slack hands, stumbling knees: people who have lost heart
decisions.reason: Hands that drop and knees that give way picture discouragement and fear (Job 4:3-4; Jeremiah 6:24). Hebrews 12:12 takes up these words to encourage weary believers.

decisions.choice: strengthen, make firm: commands to a group that is not named
decisions.reason: The verbs are plural. Whoever hears the promise is told to pass on courage to those who are weak, as in 40:1.

decisions.choice: Help people whose hands are weak ...
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the hands and knees belong to people who need help.

source.text: אִמְרוּ֙ לְנִמְהֲרֵי־לֵ֔ב חִזְק֖וּ אַל־תִּירָ֑אוּ הִנֵּ֤ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶם֙ נָקָ֣ם יָב֔וֹא גְּמ֣וּל אֱלֹהִ֔ים ה֥וּא יָב֖וֹא וְיֹשַׁעֲכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Say to [those] hasty of heart: Be strong, do not fear; look, your God: vengeance will come, the repayment of God; he will come and save you.

en.L: Say to [those] hasty of heart, "Be strong, do not fear! Look, your God! Vengeance will come, the repayment of God; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will come and save you."
en.B: Tell those whose hearts are racing, "Take courage; do not be afraid! Here is your God. Vengeance is coming, God's own repayment; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} is coming, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will save you."
en.R: Say to people who are afraid, "Be strong! Do not be afraid! Look, your God is coming! He is coming to punish {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies and pay them back. He is coming to save you."

decisions.choice: hasty of heart: anxious, in a panic
decisions.reason: A heart that hurries is one that cannot be still for fear (compare 32:4). The words that follow, "be strong, do not fear", answer that fear.

decisions.choice: vengeance, repayment: God comes to set wrongs right for his people
decisions.reason: The vengeance of 34:8 falls on the oppressors; here it means rescue for the oppressed. "Here is your God" is the same cry as 40:9.

decisions.choice: to punish his enemies and pay them back
decisions.reason: Readable says who the vengeance is against, as 34:8 makes clear.

source.text: אָ֥ז תִּפָּקַ֖חְנָה עֵינֵ֣י עִוְרִ֑ים וְאָזְנֵ֥י חֵרְשִׁ֖ים תִּפָּתַֽחְנָה׃

records.literal_gloss: Then will be opened [the] eyes of blind [ones], and [the] ears of deaf [ones] will be unstopped.

en.L: Then [the] eyes of [the] blind will be opened, and [the] ears of [the] deaf will be unstopped.
en.B: Then eyes that were blind will be opened, and ears that were deaf will be unsealed.
en.R: Then people who are blind will be able to see. People who are deaf will be able to hear.

decisions.choice: the blind and the deaf: signs of God's coming, pointed to by Jesus
decisions.reason: When John the Baptizer asked whether Jesus was the one to come, Jesus answered with this list: the blind see, the lame walk, the deaf hear (Matthew 11:5; Luke 7:22). Compare 29:18 and 42:7.

decisions.choice: opened, unstopped: a reversal of the hardening in 6:10
decisions.reason: In 6:10 the people's eyes were smeared shut and their ears made heavy. Here God's coming heals both the body and the people's dullness toward him.

source.text: אָ֣ז יְדַלֵּ֤ג כָּֽאַיָּל֙ פִּסֵּ֔חַ וְתָרֹ֖ן לְשׁ֣וֹן אִלֵּ֑ם כִּֽי־נִבְקְע֤וּ בַמִּדְבָּר֙ מַ֔יִם וּנְחָלִ֖ים בָּעֲרָבָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Then will leap like the deer [the] lame, and will shout for joy [the] tongue of [the] mute; for will break out in the wilderness waters, and streams in the desert-plain.

en.L: Then [the] lame will leap like the deer, and [the] tongue of [the] mute will shout for joy; for waters will break out in the wilderness, and streams in the desert plain.
en.B: Then the lame will spring like a deer, and the tongue of the mute will cry out with joy. For in the wilderness water will burst out, and in the barren plain, streams.
en.R: People who cannot walk will jump like deer. People who cannot speak will shout for joy. Water will flow in the desert. Streams will run through the dry land.

decisions.choice: the lame leap, the mute shout
decisions.reason: Jesus' answer to John includes the lame walking (Matthew 11:5), and the lame man healed at the temple went in leaping and praising God (Acts 3:8).

decisions.choice: streams: flowing water in dry valleys
decisions.reason: The word is used of a wadi, a valley that runs with water only after rain. Here such streams flow in the desert itself, so the healing of people and the healing of the land belong together.

decisions.choice: People who cannot walk ... People who cannot speak
decisions.reason: Readable describes the people instead of using older words for their disabilities.

source.text: וְהָיָ֤ה הַשָּׁרָב֙ לַאֲגַ֔ם וְצִמָּא֖וֹן לְמַבּ֣וּעֵי מָ֑יִם בִּנְוֵ֤ה תַנִּים֙ רִבְצָ֔הּ חָצִ֖יר לְקָנֶ֥ה וָגֹֽמֶא׃

records.literal_gloss: And will become the burning-sand a pool, and thirsty-ground springs of water; in [the] haunt of jackals, its resting-place, grass to reed and papyrus.

en.L: And the burning sand will become a pool, and [the] thirsty ground springs of water; in [the] haunt of jackals, its lair, grass [will become] reed and papyrus.
en.B: The shimmering sand will turn into a pond, and parched ground into springs of water. Where jackals once had their lairs and lay at rest, grass will give way to reeds and papyrus.
en.R: The hot, dry sand will become a pool of water. The thirsty ground will have springs of water. In places where jackals used to rest, reeds and papyrus will grow instead of grass.

decisions.choice: the burning sand: ground that shimmers with heat
decisions.reason: The word occurs again only in 49:10, for scorching heat. A related word in other Semitic languages means a mirage; if that is meant, the water that only seemed to be there becomes real.

decisions.choice: grass will become reeds and papyrus
decisions.reason: Here the word is "grass" (compare 34:13, where a word spelled the same means an abode). Reeds and papyrus need standing water (Job 8:11), so dry grassland becomes marsh.

decisions.choice: the haunt of jackals: a reversal of 34:13
decisions.reason: Edom became a haunt of jackals (34:13); here the haunts of jackals become well watered.

source.text: וְהָיָה־שָׁ֞ם מַסְל֣וּל וָדֶ֗רֶךְ וְדֶ֤רֶךְ הַקֹּ֨דֶשׁ֙ יִקָּ֣רֵא לָ֔הּ לֹֽא־יַעַבְרֶ֥נּוּ טָמֵ֖א וְהוּא־לָ֑מוֹ הֹלֵ֥ךְ דֶּ֛רֶךְ וֶאֱוִילִ֖ים לֹ֥א יִתְעֽוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And will be there a highway and a way, and the way of holiness it will be called; not will pass over it [the] unclean, and it [is] for them, one walking [the] way, and fools not will wander.

en.L: And a highway will be there, and a way, and it will be called [the] Way of Holiness. [The] unclean will not pass over it; and it [will be] for them, [for] the one walking [the] way, and fools will not wander [on it].
en.B: A raised road will run there, a highway, and it will be named the Way of Holiness. No one unclean will travel on it; it will be for those who walk the way, and fools will not stray onto it.
en.R: A main road will go through there. It will be called the Holy Way. People who are not pure will not travel on it. It will be for those who walk on that road. Foolish people will not wander onto it.

decisions.choice: the Way of Holiness: the road that belongs to the Holy One
decisions.reason: The road is holy because it belongs to the holy God and leads to him in Zion (v. 10). Those who walk it are made clean, as no unclean person will enter Zion in 52:1. Raised highways for the return come also in 11:16, 40:3 and 62:10.

decisions.choice: fools will not wander onto it
alternatives: even fools will not go astray on it
decisions.reason: The last clause is hard. It may mean that fools will not roam on the road, matching "the unclean will not pass over it". Or it may mean that the road is so plain that even simple travelers will not lose their way.

decisions.choice: a highway and a way: the received text is kept
decisions.reason: The received text has "way" twice. The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa-a) has it only once, and the first "and a way" may have been copied twice by mistake. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: the Holy Way
decisions.reason: Readable shortens "the Way of Holiness" to plain words with the same meaning.

source.text: לֹא־יִהְיֶ֨ה שָׁ֜ם אַרְיֵ֗ה וּפְרִ֤יץ חַיּוֹת֙ בַּֽל־יַעֲלֶ֔נָּה לֹ֥א תִמָּצֵ֖א שָׁ֑ם וְהָלְכ֖וּ גְּאוּלִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Not will be there a lion, and a violent one of beasts not will go up on it, not it will be found there; and will walk [the] redeemed.

en.L: No lion will be there, and [no] violent one of [the] beasts will go up on it; it will not be found there; but [the] redeemed will walk [there].
en.B: There will be no lion on it; no savage beast will set foot on it or be found there. Along it the redeemed will walk.
en.R: There will be no lions there. No dangerous wild animals will come onto the road. The people God has rescued will walk on it.

decisions.choice: lion, savage beast: dangers to travelers
decisions.reason: Lions and other beasts made desert roads dangerous (1 Kings 13:24; 30:6). On this road the travelers are safe, as in 11:6-9 and 65:25.

decisions.choice: the redeemed: people set free by the one who has the right to buy them back
decisions.reason: The word comes from the duty of a near relative to buy back a family member or land (Leviticus 25:25). The LORD is Israel's Redeemer (41:14; 43:1), and those he frees from exile walk home (51:10-11).

decisions.choice: The people God has rescued
decisions.reason: Readable says who redeems them and explains the word.

source.text: וּפְדוּיֵ֨י יְהוָ֜ה יְשֻׁב֗וּן וּבָ֤אוּ צִיּוֹן֙ בְּרִנָּ֔ה וְשִׂמְחַ֥ת עוֹלָ֖ם עַל־רֹאשָׁ֑ם שָׂשׂ֤וֹן וְשִׂמְחָה֙ יַשִּׂ֔יגוּ וְנָ֖סוּ יָג֥וֹן וַאֲנָחָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And [the] ransomed of the LORD will return and come [to] Zion with a shout of joy, and joy of forever upon their head; gladness and joy they will overtake, and will flee sorrow and sighing.

en.L: And [the] ransomed of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will return and come [to] Zion with a shout of joy, and everlasting joy [will be] upon their heads; gladness and joy will overtake [them], and sorrow and sighing will flee.
en.B: Those {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has ransomed will come back; they will enter Zion with glad shouts, with joy that never ends resting on their heads. Delight and gladness will catch up with them, and grief and groaning will run away.
en.R: The people {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has set free will come home. They will enter Zion singing and shouting. Their joy will last forever, and everyone will see it on them. Happiness and joy will catch up with them. Sadness and crying will run away.

decisions.choice: ransomed: set free at a price
decisions.reason: The verb is used of buying a person out of slavery (Exodus 21:8) and of God freeing Israel from Egypt (Deuteronomy 7:8). Here it is the return of God's people to Zion. 51:11 repeats this verse almost word for word.

decisions.choice: joy upon their heads: joy worn openly, like a garland
decisions.reason: Mourners put dust or ashes on their heads (2 Samuel 13:19); here joy rests there instead, as a beautiful headdress replaces ashes in 61:3.

decisions.choice: gladness and joy will overtake them
alternatives: they will obtain gladness and joy
decisions.reason: The verb means to reach or overtake. Either gladness and joy catch up with the travelers, or the travelers reach gladness and joy; the picture of sorrow running away suits the first.

decisions.choice: Their joy will last forever, and everyone will see it on them
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of joy resting on their heads.
